newsitem.title: UK: HORSE RACING-DETTORI LOSER ENDS BOOKMAKERS' NIGHTMARE.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-DETTORI LOSER ENDS BOOKMAKERS' NIGHTMARE.

text.p: Frankie Dettori's historic winning run came to an end in the first race at Ascot on Sunday as bookmakers heaved a mass sigh of relief.
In an astonishing and unprecedented display on Saturday, Dettori won all seven races on a high-class card at cumulative odds of over 25,000-1.
It thrilled the punters who backed him, creating three half-millionaires, but stung the bookmaking industry for an estimated 18 million pounds ($28 million) on the blackest day yet in their industry.
On Sunday, the crowds turned up looking for more of the same but it was not to be and Dettori failed to get a winner until his seventh and last ride of the day.
In the opening race, Dettori made the early running on Sunbeam Dance, a 7-2 shot.
But it was obvious from over a furlong out he would not be making it eight out of eight and the combination trailed in fourth behind 9-2 chance Kahal, ridden by Richard Hills.
The defeat ended Dettori's chance of chasing a record set in August 1933 by Sir Gordon Richards who rode 12 winners in succession, spread over three days.
Another defeat followed for Dettori in the second race, fifth of eight on Medaaly behind Benny The Dip, the mount of Walter Swinburn.

Victory looked a distinct possibility in the third on Hal's Pal, the 6-1 favourite, but the Italian-born jockey was denied in the closing stages by 33-1 chance Amrak Ajeeb as bookmakers retrieved a little of Saturday's losses.
Winning jockey Mark Rimmer said: "I could see Frankie in front but I had plenty of horse under me."
There was no joy either in the big race, the group one Fillies' Mile, when Dettori's mount Logic never got in a blow behind 5-1 winner Reams of Verse, ridden by Michael Kinane.
Dettori placed 10th and fourth in his next two rides but finally got his winner on Altamura in the Harvest Stakes.
"I am pleased I haven't lost it even though I had to wait until the lucky last," he said. "Yesterday was a great achievement and, unfortunately, the dream stopped in the first race."
